newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysian PM lashes out at currency speculators.
newsitem.headline: Malaysian PM lashes out at currency speculators.

text.p: Malaysian Prime Minister Mahathir Mohamad on Thursday launched a bitter attack on "rogue speculators" whom he accused of undermining Southeast Asian economies by destabilising their currencies.

Opening the 30th foreign ministerial meetings of the Association of South East Asian Nations (ASEAN), Mahathir said: "We see a well-planned effort to undermine the economies of all the ASEAN countries by destabilising their currencies.
"Our economic fundamentals are good, yet anyone with a few billion dollars can destroy all the progress that we have made," he said.
Malaysia and neighbouring countries have seen attacks on their currencies in the past month, forcing devaluations in Thailand and the Philippines and expensive intervention efforts in Malaysia.

On Thursday, regional currencies dropped to new lows as speculators and corporates continued to pile into the dollar, triggering stop-loss orders. No signs of central bank intervention were yet detected on Thursday.

The Thai baht dropped to a low of 32.63/dollar onshore, the Singapore dollar fell below the psychological level of 1.4700 on stop-loss sales while the Malaysian ringgit breached the 2.65 barrier in early trade on spillover weakness from Thailand and Singapore.
The Indonesian rupiah slipped back through the 2,600 support level on Thursday.
Mahathir, known for his sharp-tongued criticisms of the West, said the countries of the region were told they must open up their markets and that trade and commerce must be totally free.

"Free for whom? For rogue speculators. For anarchists wanting to destroy weak countries in their crusade for open societies, to force us to submit to the dictatorship of international manipulators," Mahathir told the ASEAN gathering.
"We want to embrace borderlessness but we still need to protect ourselves from self serving rogues and international brigandage," he said.
Mahathir did not mention any speculators by name in his speech.

Malaysia is the current chairman of ASEAN, which was expanded on Wednesday to nine members with the inclusion of Laos and Burma. Its other members are Thailand, Vietnam, the Philippines, Indonesia, Brunei and Singapore.
